arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Robert Peck argued Congress managed jurisdiction boundaries. He stated the statute had two specific goals.
Lamken argued the tolling provision is constitutional. He claimed it reflects distinct federal legal events.
Lindemann argued Congress intruded on state sovereignty. He stated the case involves more than tolling.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the reach of federal supplemental jurisdiction. It asks if federal law can pause state time limits for claims dismissed in federal court.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the boundary between federal and state power. It determines whether federal courts can extend state time limits. The outcome shapes the scope of federal jurisdiction over state claims.
